title: Chipotle Chicken Burrito Bowls
seoTitle: Chipotle Chicken Burrito Bowls | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Smoky chicken, rice, beans, fajita vegetables, and full burrito toppings
subtitle: Smoky chicken, rice, beans, fajita vegetables, and full burrito toppings
description: Chipotle chicken with cilantro-lime rice, black beans, fajita vegetables, roasted corn, pico, guacamole, sour cream, cheddar, and cilantro.

steps.title: Marinate the chicken and cut the fajita veg
steps.instruction: In a large bowl, coat boneless chicken thighs with 4 tablespoons chipotle in adobo, lime juice, oil, cumin, and salt. Slice peppers and onions into even strips and drain the black beans. Portion pico, guacamole, sour cream, and cheddar into cold pans. Measure the adobo — dumping extra from the can makes the whole batch bitter and too hot for half the crew.

steps.title: Steam the cilantro-lime rice
steps.instruction: Rinse 3 cups rice until the water runs mostly clear. Bring to a boil with 5 1/2 cups salted water in a heavy pot, cover, and cook on low 18 minutes without lifting the lid. Rest 10 minutes, fluff, then fold in lime juice and chopped cilantro. Peeking every few minutes releases steam and leaves crunchy grains on top.

steps.title: Sear the chipotle chicken
steps.instruction: Heat a large skillet or flat-top over medium-high until a drop of water skitters. Add a thin film of oil, then lay thighs in a single layer without crowding — work in batches if needed. Sear 5–6 minutes undisturbed until deep brown on the first side, flip, and cook another 5–6 minutes until the thickest piece hits 165°F. Crowding steams the chicken and you lose the smoky crust.

steps.title: Rest and slice the thighs
steps.instruction: Move cooked chicken to a clean cutting board, tent loosely with foil, and rest 5 minutes. Slice across the grain into bite-size strips and toss with any chipotle pan juices left in the skillet. Slice too early and the juices run out; skip the rest and dry chicken ends up in the bowl.

steps.title: Cook fajita peppers and warm the beans
steps.instruction: In a second screaming-hot skillet, cook pepper and onion strips with a little oil for 6–8 minutes until softened with charred edges. Do not salt them at the start — salt pulls water and stops the fajita browning. Warm beans and corn in separate small pots with a splash of water over medium-low for 5 minutes until hot.

steps.title: Set the burrito cold sauces
steps.instruction: Loosen sour cream with a squeeze of lime so it drizzles. Spoon guacamole into a bowl and press plastic wrap directly on the surface. If pico is watery, set it in a strainer over a bowl for 5 minutes. Keep all three on ice — heat browns guacamole and splits sour cream fast.

steps.title: Hold the hot burrito components
steps.instruction: Move rice, sliced chicken, fajita vegetables, beans, and corn into covered hotel pans and hold at 200°F above 140°F. Taste one piece of chicken with rice before the line opens — adjust salt or a squeeze of lime now, not after ten bowls are already built. Target oven/smoker temperature: 200°F.

steps.title: Build the burrito bowls in layers
steps.instruction: Scoop cilantro-lime rice into each bowl, then add beans, corn, and fajita peppers. Top with a measured pile of sliced chipotle chicken. Keep guacamole and sour cream off until garnish so they stay cold against the hot chicken.

steps.title: Finish with cold burrito toppings
steps.instruction: Add pico, a scoop of guacamole, a drizzle of lime sour cream, and shredded cheddar. Scatter cilantro and set a lime wedge on the rim. Guacamole and sour cream go after the chicken so the contrast stays cold and clean — not melted into the rice.

steps.title: Serve the burrito bar
steps.instruction: Send bowls with chips and extra hot sauce at the end of the table. Keep covered chicken and rice behind you for late arrivals. Use separate tongs for chicken and vegetables so the line stays clean, and refill pico in small amounts so it does not flood the service table.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-cook: turn off direct heat and cover the chipotle chicken — hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven, never below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Log hold time on the pan with a grease pencil. Keep the pico, guacamole, and sour cream on ice the whole time — heat browns guacamole and splits sour cream within minutes. On return, spot-check the chicken at a safe internal temp, then add the cold toppings fresh so the contrast still holds.

steps.title: Pack down leftovers safely
steps.instruction: Cool chipotle chicken and hot components in shallow hotel pans within two hours — deep pots stay in the danger zone too long. Label with date; reheat proteins to 165°F minimum before second shift. Store cold components separately so textures survive overnight.

proTips: Prep tip: Taste one piece of chicken before sending the heat level to the whole crew.
Rookie tip: Slice thighs after resting so the meat stays juicy.
Rookie tip: Keep pico in a strainer over a bowl if it is especially wet.
Prep tip: Use separate tongs for chicken and vegetables to keep the line clean.
Measure the adobo — extra from the can turns the whole pan bitter.
tonightSpread: Condiments: Guacamole, sour cream, chipotle hot sauce
Set hot components closest to the crew; cold crunch and toppings at the far end of the line.
Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a run.
leftovers: Cool chipotle chicken in shallow pans within two hours; label with date and reheat to 165°F before second shift.
Store cold sides separately — hot and cold stacked overnight ruins texture.
Roll leftover chicken, rice, beans, and cheese into freezer burritos.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The bowl bar gives the crew restaurant-style choice, while chicken, rice, and beans make it filling enough for a long shift.
mealPrepNotes: Make-ahead: marinate chicken, make pico, and cook beans one day ahead. Storage: cool chicken, rice, beans, and vegetables separately for 3 days; guacamole is best within 24 hours. Reheating: cover hot components with a splash of water and heat to 165°F; add cold toppings afterward.
substitutions: Use pinto beans for black beans.
Use shredded Monterey Jack for cheddar.
Use salsa verde instead of chipotle adobo.
